summary: Calibrate academic language to the strongest verified evidence actually available.
instructions: Distinguish measured, associated, indicated, causal, and generalized claims.
Do not use novelty, first, superior, robust, or general claims without the corresponding closest-work or experiment evidence.
Missing evidence routes back to research or experiments; prose must not manufacture support.
Keep public labels semantic; internal B/E/A identifiers may remain only as traceable metadata.
